createdBy: codex code review (T-008 round 4), filed by Claude
impact: Requirements the v0.2 re-spec drafts must satisfy (absorbs ISS-033). T-010: delete the pid/start-time/owner-token and inode-revalidation language (Description + Constraints). Publish = atomic rename of one self-contained temp file; no lock for structural integrity; single-writer topology is T-011's port-singleton service. Findings §3.5 obligations are binding verbatim: (1) every publisher calls assertHeld() immediately before its atomic commit with no awaits between; (2) onLost must terminate the process or irreversibly disable publishing — returning quietly is not allowed; (3) the suite carries a mutant whose publish path omits (1) and must fail. Dominance manifest = per-source offsets with incomparable-fails-closed (never a scalar max); monotonicity is advisory — worst case a stale-but-complete snapshot self-corrected by the next dominating publish. DURABILITY: settle the fsync conflict explicitly in ONE direction — T-010's write-gen→fsync-gen→write+fsync-manifest-temp→rename→fsync-parent ladder vs the findings' recorded decision that snapshots are a derived cache (process-crash atomic, NOT power-loss durable, no fsync) while coordination state (allocation + token, including the link) IS fsynced; ISS-040's rename-commit-boundary rule applies regardless. T-011: delete the lockfile state machine, the pid/start-time/token failure mode, criterion 5's inode-revalidation test, criterion 8's 'lockfile owner token', and the A-vs-B dependency wording. Replace with candidate C: write-once port allocation published via link(), validated fail-closed (owner, type, encoding, mode exactly 0600 masked 0o7777, any non-privileged port), never repaired in place, never auto re-allocated; the publication winner's provisional listener IS the lock (adopt, no close-and-rebind gap); startSingleton() composes EADDRINUSE → identifyHolder() → decision — foreign or unidentifiable holder throws PortLockForeignHolder with the allocation file byte-identical afterwards; domain-separated challenge–response (protocol id + required non-empty purpose + allocationId + challenger's 256-bit length-framed nonce, reply at the request boundary); unexpected close raises a named lock-loss witness and the lock is single-use; credential fallback = 0700 runtime dir validated as the primary isolation boundary (lstat type, owner uid, non-symlink, mode exactly 0700 masked 0o7777) + 32-byte 0600 token published write-once via link() with directory fsync + digest-based timingSafeEqual; socket path uid-keyed short-by-construction, rejected BEFORE listen when canonical byte length > 104, symlinks strictly below the canonicalized root and dot/dot-dot/empty components refused; fixed startup order (handover 2026-08-01-04): validate write-once token → validate write-once allocation → acquire port → probe unix socket → reclaim only confirmed-stale → bind socket → serve. No-PID-control stands, but the guard is the port bind, not a PID record. T-012: replace 'inode revalidation before every publish applies to every fast tick' with: every fast-tier publish goes through the singleton's assertHeld-guarded commit; a tick that observed lock loss discards its shadow work. KEEP the shadow pre/post inode/size/mtime validation — that is file-change detection, not lock language (ISS-033's keyword count overstated T-012). Also require an async cancellable subprocess boundary for service-tier ccusage runs — src/runner.ts is spawnSync-based (lines 14, 176) and would block the daemon event loop for 60–80 s. T-013: replace expiry/takeover/ownership-record language with: the reader computation lease is the same primitive on its OWN write-once allocation + required non-empty purpose (domain separation so a reader lease can never impersonate the writer singleton); no ownership records, no expiry, no timeout takeover (that recreates the split-owner race) — holder death frees the port and contenders re-bid the persisted port; a live-but-hung holder gets bounded-wait-then-honest-stale; leases are an optimization, not a correctness boundary (findings §3.3). Fold in N-003's delegated decisions: @modelcontextprotocol/server@2.0.0 exact-pinned + zod exact direct enter the root manifest only when src/mcp lands; token budget = measured T-013 baseline +10% as a CI hard gate. T-014 (minor): replace the false 'spikes/ contains only spikes/rounding' inventory with the direct fact: no Swift helper prototype source is committed.
resolution: Fixed by the v0.2/v0.3 ticket re-spec applied 2026-08-02: T-010/T-011/T-012/T-013 (and T-014's stale spikes inventory) now specify T-008's adopted candidate C — write-once port allocation + provisional-listener lock, assertHeld-before-commit, loss-witness obligations — with every lockfile/inode-revalidation passage removed. The T-010 fsync conflict is settled in the findings' recorded direction: snapshots are a derived cache (no fsync, rename is the commit boundary, asserted by test); coordination state stays fsynced. The full verified requirements record is preserved in this issue's impact field.
title: T-010/T-011/T-012/T-013 still specify the lockfile architecture T-008 rejected
